title: Speculative Decoding for Masked Diffusion Language Models via Draft-and-Refine Sampling
description:
Problem: LLaDA and similar masked diffusion LMs (MDLMs) suffer from slow inference because they require multiple forward passes (denoising steps) through a large Transformer to generate text, making them impractical for real-time applications despite their strong capabilities. Unlike autoregressive models, existing speculative decoding techniques cannot be directly applied since MDLMs operate on the full sequence simultaneously across discrete diffusion timesteps.

Proposed Method: We introduce DiffSpec, a speculative decoding framework tailored for MDLMs. A small draft MDLM (e.g., 1B parameters) runs several denoising steps to produce a partially-denoised candidate sequence. A large verifier MDLM (e.g., 8B parameters) then evaluates the draft in a single forward pass, accepting high-confidence token predictions and re-masking uncertain positions for targeted refinement. We derive an acceptance criterion grounded in the MDLM likelihood lower bound, ensuring the output distribution approximates that of the verifier alone. We also propose an adaptive masking schedule that concentrates verifier compute on ambiguous tokens.

Experiments: We evaluate on LLaDA 8B with a 1B draft model across generation benchmarks (MT-Bench, HumanEval, GSM8K), measuring wall-clock speedup and quality degradation versus solo verifier decoding. We compare against naive step-reduction baselines and analyze acceptance rates across diffusion timesteps and task types.

title: Speculative Decoding for Masked Diffusion Language Models via Draft-and-Denoise
description:
Problem: While LLaDA demonstrates that masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) achieve competitive quality with autoregressive models, their inference remains slow due to requiring many sequential denoising steps, each involving a full forward pass through a large Transformer. Unlike ARMs, MDLMs cannot leverage existing speculative decoding frameworks designed for next-token prediction.

Proposed Method: We introduce Draft-and-Denoise (D&D), a speculative acceleration framework tailored for MDLMs. A small, fast draft MDLM proposes a partially-denoised token sequence given the current noise level. A large verifier MDLM then accepts or rejects proposed tokens in parallel using a mask-diffusion-aware acceptance criterion derived from the ratio of denoising distributions, preserving the exact marginal distribution of the large model. We further propose an adaptive step-skipping schedule that uses draft confidence scores to dynamically merge multiple denoising steps, reducing total NFEs (number of function evaluations) without quality degradation.

Experiments: (1) Throughput benchmarks on LLaDA 8B across text generation, math (GSM8K), and code (HumanEval) tasks measuring tokens/second vs. baseline MDLM sampling. (2) Quality preservation tests via MT-Bench and perplexity to verify distribution matching. (3) Ablations on draft model size, acceptance threshold, and step-skipping aggressiveness. We target 2-4x wall-clock speedup with <1% quality degradation.

title: SpecDiff: Accelerating Large Language Diffusion Models via Speculative Decoding with Autoregressive Draft Models
description: Problem: Despite LLaDA's competitive performance, masked diffusion language models suffer from high inference latency because they require multiple full forward passes through a large Transformer to iteratively unmask tokens, making deployment impractical compared to ARM-based LLMs with KV-cache acceleration. Proposed Method: We introduce SpecDiff, a speculative decoding framework tailored for masked diffusion LLMs. A small, fast ARM (draft model) proposes candidate token sequences, which are then verified and corrected in parallel by the diffusion model (verifier) in a single forward pass. We develop a novel acceptance-rejection scheme that respects the diffusion model's token-level confidence scores and masking schedule, allowing the verifier to selectively accept draft tokens and re-mask rejected positions for refinement. We also propose an adaptive step-skipping heuristic that reduces the number of diffusion denoising steps based on draft quality. Experiments: (1) Throughput benchmarks on LLaDA-8B across diverse tasks (MT-Bench, GSM8K, HumanEval) measuring tokens/second versus quality tradeoff; (2) Ablations comparing draft model sizes (125M, 1B ARM) and acceptance thresholds; (3) Quality-latency Pareto curves comparing SpecDiff to baseline diffusion decoding and standard ARM generation; (4) Analysis of acceptance rates across task types to characterize when ARM drafts align with diffusion model preferences.

title: Speculative Decoding for Masked Diffusion Language Models via Draft-then-Denoise
description: Problem: Unlike autoregressive models, masked diffusion language models (e.g., LLaDA) must perform multiple full forward passes through a large Transformer to iteratively unmask tokens, making inference significantly slower than ARM counterparts. No efficient speculative execution framework exists for this paradigm. Proposed Method: We introduce Speculative Diffusion Decoding (SDD), a framework that uses a small draft diffusion model to propose partially-denoised token sequences in fewer steps, which are then verified and corrected by the large target diffusion model in parallel. Specifically, the draft model runs K diffusion steps to produce a candidate sequence; the target model evaluates the entire sequence in one forward pass, accepting tokens whose predicted marginal distributions closely match (via a KL-divergence threshold) and re-sampling only rejected positions. We additionally propose an adaptive step-skipping schedule that dynamically allocates diffusion steps based on per-token uncertainty estimates, reducing redundant computation in already-confident positions. Experiments: We benchmark SDD on LLaDA 8B against naive MDLM inference on standard benchmarks (LAMBADA, HumanEval, GSM8K, MT-Bench), measuring wall-clock speedup, token acceptance rates, and quality degradation. We compare against ARM speculative decoding baselines and ablate draft model size (70M, 1B, 3B) and acceptance thresholds to characterize the efficiency-quality tradeoff.

title: Speculative Decoding for Masked Diffusion Language Models via Draft-and-Denoise
description: Problem: Despite LLaDA's competitive quality, masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) suffer from slow inference because they require many sequential denoising steps (e.g., 64–256 forward passes through a large Transformer), making them impractical for deployment compared to single-pass autoregressive models. Unlike ARMs, existing speculative decoding techniques are inapplicable since MDLMs have no notion of token-by-token generation or a draft sequence in the autoregressive sense. Proposed Method: We introduce Speculative Denoising (SpecDenoise), a framework that pairs a small MDLM 'draft' model with a large MDLM 'verifier'. The draft model runs many denoising steps cheaply to produce a partially or fully unmasked candidate sequence. The verifier then evaluates all token positions in parallel via a single forward pass, accepting positions where the draft's confidence exceeds a learned threshold and re-masking uncertain positions for targeted re-denoising. We derive acceptance criteria that preserve the verifier's marginal distribution and propose an adaptive masking schedule that concentrates verifier compute on high-uncertainty tokens. Experiments: We benchmark SpecDenoise using LLaDA 1B as draft and LLaDA 8B as verifier on MT-Bench, GSM8K, HumanEval, and a latency-throughput Pareto analysis, comparing against naive step-reduction baselines and measuring quality-speed tradeoffs across decoding step budgets.

title: Speculative Diffusion Decoding: Accelerating Masked Diffusion Language Models via Lightweight Draft Models
description:
Problem: Despite strong capabilities, masked diffusion language models like LLaDA suffer from slow inference because they require many iterative denoising steps over the full sequence, unlike autoregressive models where speculative decoding with draft models provides significant speedups. There is no established framework to accelerate diffusion LLMs at inference time.

Proposed Method: We introduce Speculative Diffusion Decoding (SDD), a framework that pairs a large masked diffusion model (the verifier) with a small, fast draft model—either a tiny masked diffusion model or a lightweight ARM. At each denoising step, the draft model proposes token assignments for all masked positions simultaneously; the large verifier then scores and selectively accepts or rejects these proposals based on a token-level acceptance criterion derived from the likelihood ratio between verifier and draft distributions. Rejected tokens are re-masked and resampled by the verifier. We additionally explore training the draft model with a distillation objective aligned to the verifier's marginal distributions.

Experiments: (1) Measure wall-clock speedup and quality (perplexity, benchmark accuracy) on LLaDA 8B across text generation tasks. (2) Ablate draft model size, acceptance thresholds, and number of denoising steps. (3) Compare against step-reduction baselines (fewer NFE schedules). (4) Evaluate on math reasoning and instruction-following to confirm quality preservation. Target: 2-3x speedup with <1% benchmark degradation.

title: SpecDiff: Accelerating Large Language Diffusion Models via Speculative Masked Decoding
description: Problem: LLaDA and similar masked diffusion LLMs suffer from slow inference because they require many sequential denoising steps (typically 64-128 forward passes), each processing the full sequence. Unlike autoregressive models, they cannot easily exploit KV-caching or speculative decoding in standard forms, making deployment impractical compared to ARM counterparts of similar scale. Proposed Method: We introduce SpecDiff, a speculative decoding framework tailored for masked diffusion LLMs. A small 'draft' diffusion model (e.g., 1B parameters) proposes token fills for multiple denoising steps simultaneously, while the large 'verifier' model (e.g., 8B) validates and corrects accepted tokens in a single forward pass using a novel diffusion-compatible acceptance criterion derived from the masked token likelihood ratio. Additionally, we propose an adaptive step-skipping scheduler that dynamically predicts which denoising steps can be collapsed based on token uncertainty entropy, reducing effective steps from 128 to ~20 without quality degradation. Experiments: We evaluate on LLaDA-8B across standard benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K, HumanEval), measuring wall-clock speedup (target: 4-6x), token acceptance rates, and quality degradation (target: <1% relative drop). We compare against naive step-reduction baselines and ARM speculative decoding, and analyze the acceptance rate versus draft model size trade-off.

title: DiffuCode: Masked Diffusion Language Models for Repository-Level Code Generation with Bidirectional Context Integration
description:
Problem: Autoregressive models struggle with repository-level code generation because completing functions deep within a codebase requires reasoning about both preceding context (imports, prior functions) and subsequent usage (function calls, tests that follow). The causal left-to-right constraint of ARMs prevents native exploitation of right-side context without awkward prompt engineering. Masked diffusion language models like LLaDA naturally support bidirectional conditioning, making them potentially superior for fill-in-the-middle (FIM) code synthesis tasks.

Proposed Method: We fine-tune LLaDA 8B on a curated repository-level code corpus (The Stack v2, filtered for Python/Java/TypeScript) using a specialized masking curriculum: early training masks contiguous code spans (functions, classes), while later stages mask semantically critical tokens (API calls, variable names, type annotations). We introduce a 'context-aware noise schedule' that masks code regions proportionally to their cross-file dependency depth, forcing the model to learn repository-level coherence. At inference, we incorporate retrieved relevant code snippets as unmasked conditioning tokens.

Experiments: Evaluate on RepoBench, CrossCodeEval, and SWE-bench Lite against ARM baselines (CodeLlama, DeepSeek-Coder) and FIM-trained models. Ablate masking curriculum, context retrieval, and noise schedules. Measure exact match, CodeBLEU, and test-pass rates, with specific analysis of bidirectional context utilization versus left-context-only performance gaps.

title: SpecDiff: Speculative Decoding for Masked Diffusion Language Models via Draft-then-Denoise
description:
Problem: Despite LLaDA demonstrating that masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) rival autoregressive LLMs in quality, their inference remains slow because each denoising step requires a full forward pass through a large Transformer to unmask tokens, and typical sampling requires dozens of such steps. Unlike autoregressive models, MDLMs lack established acceleration techniques like speculative decoding.

Proposed Method: We introduce SpecDiff, a speculative decoding framework tailored for MDLMs. A small draft MDLM (e.g., 400M parameters) proposes partial unmasking across multiple diffusion steps simultaneously, predicting which tokens to unmask and their values. A large verifier MDLM (e.g., 8B parameters) then evaluates all drafted tokens in a single forward pass, accepting or rejecting each token via a masking-aware acceptance criterion derived from the ELBO objective. Rejected tokens are re-masked and re-denoised by the verifier. We further propose an adaptive step-skipping scheduler that uses the draft model's confidence to skip intermediate diffusion timesteps.

Experiments: We evaluate on standard text generation benchmarks (LAMBADA, WMT, HumanEval, GSM8K), measuring tokens-per-second speedup versus quality (perplexity, accuracy). We compare against naive MDLM sampling, ARM speculative decoding baselines, and ablate draft model size, acceptance thresholds, and step-skipping aggressiveness. Target: 2-4x wall-clock speedup with <1% quality degradation.

title: DiffRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Masked Diffusion Language Models for Knowledge-Intensive Tasks
description:
Problem: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with autoregressive LLMs suffers from positional bias—retrieved documents prepended to prompts are weighted unequally due to recency effects and left-to-right generation constraints. This causes inconsistent grounding when relevant evidence appears across multiple retrieved chunks. Masked diffusion models like LLaDA offer bidirectional context awareness during generation, potentially enabling more faithful evidence integration.

Proposed Method: We adapt LLaDA for RAG by designing a retrieval-conditioned masking schedule where tokens corresponding to answer spans are masked at higher rates while retrieved context tokens are preserved as conditioning signals. During reverse generation, the model iteratively refines answer tokens by attending bidirectionally over all retrieved passages simultaneously. We introduce a 'retrieval attention entropy' regularization term to encourage uniform evidence utilization across retrieved chunks, combating positional bias inherent in ARM-based RAG.

Experiments: (1) Evaluate on knowledge-intensive benchmarks: Natural Questions, TriviaQA, HotpotQA, and Multi-hop FEVER. (2) Compare against RAG with LLaMA3-8B and GPT-4o baselines. (3) Ablate masking schedules, number of retrieved passages (1-20), and passage ordering permutations to measure positional robustness. (4) Measure faithfulness via attribution scores. We hypothesize LLaDA-RAG shows significantly lower performance variance under passage reordering compared to ARM baselines.

title: DiffRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Masked Diffusion Language Models
description:
Problem: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems built on autoregressive LLMs suffer from position bias and sequential token commitment, making it difficult to coherently integrate retrieved evidence across long contexts. Masked diffusion language models like LLaDA offer a fundamentally different generation paradigm that iteratively refines all output tokens simultaneously, potentially enabling better global coherence when synthesizing multiple retrieved documents.

Proposed Method: We adapt LLaDA for RAG by designing a retrieval-conditioned masking and denoising framework. Specifically, we condition the reverse diffusion process on encoded retrieved passages via cross-attention, and introduce a 'relevance-guided unmasking schedule' that prioritizes unmasking tokens near high-relevance retrieved spans first. We fine-tune LLaDA 8B on standard RAG training sets (Natural Questions, TriviaQA, FEVER) with a contrastive document-grounding auxiliary loss that encourages faithfulness. We additionally explore iterative retrieval during intermediate diffusion steps, allowing the model to retrieve new evidence based on partially denoised hypotheses.

Experiments: (1) Compare against RAG-enabled LLaMA3 8B and GPT-4o on open-domain QA benchmarks measuring accuracy and faithfulness (RAGAS). (2) Multi-document synthesis tasks requiring cross-passage reasoning. (3) Ablations on unmasking schedules and iterative mid-diffusion retrieval. (4) Hallucination rate analysis. We hypothesize diffusion-based generation better handles conflicting retrieved evidence through holistic token refinement.

title: Speculative Diffusion Decoding: Accelerating Masked Diffusion Language Models via Draft-and-Verify Sampling
description:
Problem: Despite strong language modeling capabilities, masked diffusion models like LLaDA suffer from slow inference compared to autoregressive models. Each denoising step requires a full forward pass through a large Transformer to unmask tokens, and many steps are needed for high-quality generation, making practical deployment costly. Unlike ARMs, diffusion models lack established acceleration techniques like speculative decoding.

Proposed Method: We introduce Speculative Diffusion Decoding (SDD), adapting speculative execution to masked diffusion LMs. A small draft diffusion model (e.g., 1B parameters) proposes token unmaskings across multiple positions simultaneously in a single step. A large verifier model (e.g., 8B) then evaluates the joint probability of the draft's proposals in one forward pass, accepting or rejecting each proposed unmasking using a corrected acceptance criterion derived from the masked diffusion likelihood bound. Accepted tokens are fixed; rejected positions are re-masked and re-sampled. We also explore using a lightweight ARM as the drafter, exploiting its strong local token prediction.

Experiments: (1) Measure wall-clock speedup and tokens/second on LLaDA 8B across benchmarks (MT-Bench, HumanEval, GSM8K). (2) Evaluate generation quality (perplexity, task accuracy) vs. standard sampling. (3) Ablate draft model size, acceptance thresholds, and number of speculative steps. (4) Compare ARM-drafter vs. small-diffusion-drafter strategies.

title: Speculative Diffusion Decoding: Accelerating Masked Diffusion Language Models via ARM Draft Proposals
description: Problem: Large masked diffusion language models like LLaDA achieve strong generation quality but suffer significant inference latency compared to autoregressive models (ARMs). title: Speculative Decoding for Masked Diffusion Language Models via Draft-and-Refine Parallel Generation
description:

We design an acceptance criterion grounded in the marginal token probabilities of the verifier's masked diffusion objective, ensuring the output distribution remains theoretically equivalent to the large model's. We further introduce adaptive step scheduling: the draft model estimates per-position uncertainty to decide which positions to speculatively fill vs. defer.

Experiments: We benchmark DiffSpec on LLaDA 7B/8B across long-form generation (summarization, dialogue), math (GSM8K), and code (HumanEval), measuring wall-clock speedup, token acceptance rates, and quality preservation. title: Speculative Diffusion Decoding: Accelerating Masked Diffusion Language Models with Learned Draft Schedulers
description: Problem: Large masked diffusion language models like LLaDA require many denoising steps (e.g., 128 forward passes through an 8B-parameter Transformer) to generate high-quality text, making inference significantly slower than autoregressive models in tokens-per-second terms. The large model then verifies and corrects only uncertain positions, analogous to speculative decoding in ARMs but operating over the joint token distribution inherent to diffusion. We further introduce a 'confidence-gated unmasking' criterion that skips denoising steps for high-confidence tokens entirely, reducing effective NFEs (neural function evaluations) by up to 4x. Training uses a distillation objective pairing the full LLaDA 8B with the draft model on diverse generation tasks. Experiments: We benchmark on MT-Bench, HumanEval, GSM8K, and open-ended generation, measuring tokens/second, quality-compute tradeoffs, and comparing against consistency distillation and MDLM baselines. title: Controllable Constrained Generation with LLaDA: Hard Constraint Satisfaction via Masked Diffusion Planning
description:

title: Speculative Decoding for Masked Diffusion Language Models via Confidence-Guided Token Scheduling

title: DiffEdit-Code: Leveraging Masked Diffusion Language Models for Iterative Program Repair and Refinement

(2) Ablate masking strategies: random vs. syntactic vs. test-feedback-guided. (3) Measure edit locality—fraction of original correct tokens preserved—as a new metric. title: DiffRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Masked Diffusion Language Models

Experiments: We evaluate on standard RAG benchmarks (Natural Questions, TriviaQA, PopQA, 2WikiMultihopQA), comparing against ARM-based RAG systems (LLaMA3+RAG). Experiments: (1) Latency benchmarks on MT-Bench, GSM8K, and HumanEval measuring tokens/second vs. quality tradeoff; (2) ablations on skip predictor size and verification frequency; (3) comparison against uniform step-reduction baselines and consistency distillation; (4) analysis of which token positions benefit most from full denoising steps.

description: Problem: LLaDA and similar masked diffusion language models suffer from slow inference because they require multiple forward passes (denoising steps) through a large Transformer, making them impractical for latency-sensitive applications despite their strong generative capabilities. Proposed Method: We introduce SpecDiff, a speculative acceleration framework tailored for masked diffusion LMs. A small, fast autoregressive draft model proposes candidate token completions for highly masked positions in a single forward pass. The large diffusion model then acts as a verifier: in one denoising step it jointly scores all proposed tokens via its masked token prediction head, accepting high-confidence predictions and re-masking rejections. We derive an acceptance criterion grounded in the diffusion model's likelihood lower bound to ensure the output distribution remains faithful to the target model. Additionally, we propose an adaptive masking schedule that concentrates remaining denoising budget on rejected/uncertain tokens. title: Speculative Diffusion Decoding: Accelerating Masked Diffusion Language Models via Lightweight Draft Models
description:
Problem: Despite strong capabilities, masked diffusion language models like LLaDA suffer from slow inference due to requiring multiple forward passes (denoising steps) through a large transformer, making them impractical for latency-sensitive applications compared to autoregressive models with KV-cache acceleration.

Proposed Method: We introduce Speculative Diffusion Decoding (SDD), adapting speculative execution to the masked diffusion framework. A small, fast draft diffusion model proposes token unmaskings across multiple denoising steps simultaneously, while the large target model verifies and corrects these proposals in a single batched forward pass. We design a novel acceptance criterion compatible with the discrete masking schedule, ensuring the final output distribution remains identical to the target model. We further propose 'step bundling' where the draft model performs k denoising steps and the verifier corrects them jointly, exploiting the bidirectional attention structure unique to masked diffusion.

Experiments: (1) Latency benchmarks comparing SDD against standard LLaDA decoding and ARM speculative decoding on text generation tasks; (2) Throughput-quality tradeoffs varying draft model size (125M, 1B drafting for 8B target); (3) Ablations on acceptance rate vs. step bundling factor k; (4) Evaluation on LLaDA benchmarks confirming distribution preservation; (5) Comparison against alternative acceleration methods like MDLM parallel decoding heuristics. Target: 2-4x wall-clock speedup with no quality degradation.

title: Speculative Decoding for Masked Diffusion Language Models via Draft-Then-Denoise
description: Problem: While LLaDA demonstrates that masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) are competitive with autoregressive models, their inference remains slow due to requiring multiple full forward passes through a large Transformer to iteratively unmask tokens. Unlike ARMs, MDLMs lack established acceleration techniques like speculative decoding. Proposed Method: We introduce 'Draft-then-Denoise' (DtD), a speculative acceleration framework tailored for MDLMs. A small, fast draft MDLM proposes a fully-unmasked candidate sequence in a single pass. The large verifier MDLM then evaluates the draft by computing per-token acceptance probabilities based on its predicted masked token distributions in parallel, accepting or rejecting tokens according to a corrected sampling scheme that preserves the target distribution. Rejected tokens are re-masked and resampled locally, requiring only partial re-denoising steps rather than full sequence regeneration. We further propose an adaptive masking schedule for the draft model that aligns with the verifier's denoising trajectory to maximize acceptance rates. Experiments: We evaluate DtD on LLaDA-8B with a 1B draft model across reasoning (GSM8K, MATH), code (HumanEval), and dialogue benchmarks, measuring wall-clock speedup, output quality degradation, and acceptance rates. We compare against naive parallel decoding and standard MDLM inference baselines, targeting 2-4x speedup with negligible quality loss.

title: Speculative Diffusion Decoding: Accelerating Masked Diffusion Language Models via Lightweight Draft Models
description:
Problem: Large masked diffusion language models like LLaDA achieve strong performance but suffer from slow inference due to requiring multiple forward passes (denoising steps) through a large Transformer to generate text, making them impractical for latency-sensitive applications compared to autoregressive models with KV-caching.

Proposed Method: We introduce Speculative Diffusion Decoding (SDD), a framework that pairs a large masked diffusion model (the verifier) with a small, fast draft diffusion model trained on the same pretraining distribution. The draft model proposes a partially-denoised token sequence across several diffusion steps in parallel. The large verifier then evaluates the entire draft trajectory in a single forward pass, accepting tokens whose predicted distributions are sufficiently close to the verifier's distribution (via a token-level acceptance criterion adapted from speculative decoding theory for non-autoregressive settings). Rejected tokens are resampled from the verifier's distribution. We derive theoretical guarantees that SDD preserves the verifier's output distribution and analyze expected speedup as a function of draft-verifier agreement.

Experiments: We benchmark SDD on LLaDA-8B paired with a 1B draft model across (1) generation throughput on standard benchmarks (MT-Bench, HumanEval, GSM8K), (2) quality preservation via perplexity and task accuracy, and (3) ablations on draft model size, number of diffusion steps, and acceptance threshold, targeting 2-4x wall-clock speedup without quality degradation.

title: SpecDiff: Accelerating Large Language Diffusion Models via Speculative Decoding with Autoregressive Draft Models
description:
Problem: Despite LLaDA's strong capabilities, masked diffusion language models suffer from slow inference—they require multiple forward passes (typically 64–256 steps) through a large Transformer to generate sequences, making them impractical for latency-sensitive applications. Unlike autoregressive models, no efficient speculative decoding framework exists for diffusion LLMs.

Proposed Method: We introduce SpecDiff, a speculative acceleration framework tailored for masked diffusion LLMs. A small, fast autoregressive draft model proposes token candidates for still-masked positions at each diffusion step. A verification mechanism—grounded in the diffusion model's joint token probability estimates—accepts or rejects draft tokens in parallel, preserving the exact marginal distribution of the original diffusion process. We derive a theoretically principled acceptance criterion adapted from speculative sampling but modified to handle the partially-masked state space of masked diffusion. Additionally, we propose a step-skipping scheduler that uses the draft model's confidence to adaptively reduce the number of diffusion timesteps.

Experiments: (1) Throughput benchmarks on LLaDA 8B vs. baseline diffusion sampling on standard generation tasks (MT-Bench, HumanEval, GSM8K); (2) Ablations on draft model size, acceptance thresholds, and step schedules; (3) Quality-speed Pareto curves comparing SpecDiff against MDLM samplers and ARM baselines; (4) Analysis of distribution fidelity via n-gram and semantic similarity metrics to ensure lossless acceleration.

title: Speculative Decoding for Masked Diffusion Language Models via Draft-then-Denoise
description: Problem: Large masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) like LLaDA achieve strong quality but suffer from slow inference due to requiring many iterative denoising steps across all token positions simultaneously. Unlike autoregressive models, existing speculative decoding frameworks cannot directly apply since MDLMs lack a sequential token generation order. We need new acceleration strategies tailored to their parallel, iterative denoising nature. Proposed Method: We introduce 'Draft-then-Denoise' (DtD), a speculative execution framework for MDLMs. A lightweight draft model (e.g., a small 1B MDLM) performs a coarse denoising pass in few steps, proposing candidate token completions for all positions. A larger verifier MDLM (e.g., 8B) then evaluates all drafted tokens in a single forward pass, accepting high-confidence tokens and re-masking uncertain ones for targeted re-denoising. We additionally propose a confidence-adaptive masking schedule that concentrates compute on hard positions identified by the draft model, reducing total denoising steps needed in the verification model. Experiments: We benchmark DtD on LLaDA-8B against standard MDLM sampling and continuous batching baselines across MT-Bench dialogue, GSM8K, and HumanEval, measuring tokens/second, acceptance rate, and quality degradation. We also ablate draft model size and number of denoising steps to map the speed-quality Pareto frontier.

title: Speculative Diffusion Decoding: Accelerating Large Language Diffusion Models via Draft-then-Refine Masked Generation
description: Problem: Despite LLaDA's competitive performance, masked diffusion language models suffer from slow inference due to requiring many denoising steps (e.g., 128 steps), making deployment impractical compared to autoregressive models that benefit from KV-caching and speculative decoding. No efficient inference framework tailored to discrete diffusion LLMs currently exists. Proposed Method: We introduce Speculative Diffusion Decoding (SDD), a two-stage inference acceleration framework for masked diffusion LLMs. A small, fast draft diffusion model (e.g., 1B parameters) proposes partially-denoised token sequences in few steps, which a larger verifier model (e.g., LLaDA 8B) then refines or corrects in parallel using a single forward pass with targeted re-masking of low-confidence tokens. We introduce a confidence-based acceptance criterion adapted from speculative decoding theory to masked diffusion processes, proving that the output distribution remains consistent with the target model. We further develop adaptive step-skipping, where the number of refinement steps scales with draft quality estimated via token entropy. Experiments: We benchmark SDD on LLaDA 8B across standard NLP benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K, HumanEval), measuring tokens-per-second, quality degradation (perplexity, accuracy), and acceptance rates, comparing against naive step-reduction and uniform diffusion baselines. We target 3-5x wall-clock speedup with <1% quality degradation.

title: SpecDiff: Accelerating Large Language Diffusion Models via Speculative Decoding with Autoregressive Draft Models
description: Problem: Despite LLaDA's strong language modeling capabilities, masked diffusion models suffer from high inference latency because each denoising step requires a full forward pass through a large Transformer, and unlike ARMs, they cannot easily leverage KV-caching or early-exit strategies. This bottleneck limits practical deployment. Proposed Method: We introduce SpecDiff, a speculative decoding framework tailored for masked diffusion LLMs. A small, fast ARM draft model proposes candidate token sequences for partially-masked positions at each diffusion timestep. The large diffusion model then acts as a verifier, accepting or rejecting draft tokens based on a principled acceptance criterion derived from the masked diffusion likelihood. Accepted tokens are fixed early, reducing the effective number of tokens the diffusion model must rescore per step. We further propose an adaptive masking schedule that concentrates diffusion model compute on high-uncertainty token positions identified by the draft model's confidence scores. Planned Experiments: (1) Latency benchmarks on standard generation tasks comparing SpecDiff against vanilla LLaDA and MDLM baselines; (2) Quality-speed tradeoff curves on MT-Bench, GSM8K, and HumanEval; (3) Ablations on draft model size, acceptance threshold, and adaptive masking schedule; (4) Analysis of acceptance rates across token positions and diffusion timesteps to characterize when ARM drafts align with diffusion posteriors.

title: DiffSpec: Controlled Code Generation via Masked Diffusion with Formal Specification Guidance
description:
Problem: Autoregressive code generation models struggle with global constraint satisfaction — they generate token-by-token and cannot easily revise early decisions that violate downstream formal specifications (type safety, API contracts, functional correctness). LLaDA's bidirectional masked diffusion offers a natural framework for iterative refinement, but it has not been explored for specification-guided synthesis.

Proposed Method: We introduce DiffSpec, a masked diffusion language model for code generation that incorporates formal specifications as soft constraints during the reverse denoising process. At each denoising step, we augment the standard masked token prediction with a specification critic — a lightweight neural verifier trained on (code, spec, pass/fail) triples — that re-weights token probabilities to favor candidates satisfying type signatures, pre/postconditions, or unit tests. During inference, we interleave standard diffusion steps with classifier guidance signals from the spec critic, enabling global coherence without retraining the base model.

Experiments: (1) Fine-tune LLaDA 8B on competitive programming datasets with accompanying formal specs. (2) Evaluate on HumanEval+, MBPP, and a new benchmark with explicit type and contract annotations. (3) Ablate guidance strength vs. pass@k tradeoffs. (4) Compare against ARM baselines (CodeLlama, DeepSeek-Coder) and diffusion baselines without spec guidance. We hypothesize that bidirectional context allows DiffSpec to better satisfy global structural constraints than autoregressive models.

title: DiffRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Large Language Diffusion Models for Knowledge-Intensive Tasks
description:
Problem: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines currently rely almost exclusively on autoregressive LLMs as the reader/generator component. However, ARMs process retrieved documents sequentially, potentially struggling to holistically reconcile multiple retrieved passages with the query. Masked diffusion models like LLaDA can condition generation on arbitrary context positions simultaneously, suggesting a natural fit for RAG where retrieved chunks and query co-attend bidirectionally during generation. Yet no work has explored diffusion LLMs as RAG readers.

Proposed Method: We adapt LLaDA 8B as a RAG reader by (1) designing a structured prompt format that concatenates retrieved passages with the masked answer span, enabling bidirectional attention over all retrieved evidence during denoising; (2) introducing a passage-relevance-weighted masking schedule that correlates token masking probability with retrieved document relevance scores; (3) fine-tuning on knowledge-intensive QA datasets (Natural Questions, TriviaQA, PopQA) under the RAG paradigm.

Experiments: We benchmark DiffRAG against ARM-based RAG readers (LLaMA3-8B, Mistral-7B) on open-domain QA, multi-hop reasoning (HotpotQA, MuSiQue), and conflicting-evidence scenarios where retrieved passages contradict each other. We measure exact match, F1, faithfulness to retrieved context, and robustness to irrelevant passages. We hypothesize diffusion readers better integrate multi-document evidence due to bidirectional conditioning, and are more robust to retrieval noise.

title: Speculative Diffusion Decoding: Accelerating Masked Diffusion Language Models via Draft-then-Refine Generation
description:
Problem: Despite strong performance, masked diffusion language models like LLaDA suffer from slow inference because they require many sequential denoising steps (e.g., 64-128 forward passes), making them impractical for real-time applications compared to autoregressive models that benefit from KV-caching and speculative decoding.

Proposed Method: We introduce Speculative Diffusion Decoding (SDD), which pairs a small 'draft' masked diffusion model with a large 'verifier' diffusion model. The draft model rapidly proposes token candidates across multiple positions simultaneously in a small number of steps, while the verifier accepts or rejects these proposals in parallel using a novel diffusion-compatible acceptance criterion derived from the marginal likelihoods of the masked diffusion process. Unlike speculative decoding for ARMs (which is sequential), SDD exploits the inherently parallel nature of diffusion models by batching multi-position proposals into single verification passes. We additionally propose an adaptive step-skipping schedule that dynamically reduces denoising steps for high-confidence token positions.

Experiments: (1) Throughput benchmarks on LLaDA-3B/8B comparing tokens-per-second against baseline diffusion sampling and ARM baselines; (2) Quality preservation evaluation on MT-Bench, GSM8K, and HumanEval; (3) Ablation over draft model size ratios (1B/8B, 400M/8B); (4) Analysis of acceptance rates across denoising timesteps. Target: 3-5x speedup with <1% quality degradation.

title: Speculative Diffusion Decoding: Accelerating Masked Diffusion Language Models via Draft-then-Refine Sampling
description: Problem: Large masked diffusion language models like LLaDA suffer from slow inference because they require many sequential denoising steps (e.g., 128 steps), each involving a full forward pass through a large Transformer. Unlike autoregressive models where speculative decoding leverages small draft models, no analogous acceleration framework exists for diffusion LMs. Proposed Method: We introduce Speculative Diffusion Decoding (SDD), a framework that uses a small, fast masked diffusion draft model to propose token assignments across multiple positions simultaneously, which are then verified/corrected in parallel by the large target diffusion model. Crucially, we exploit the bidirectional nature of diffusion LMs: the verifier can evaluate all proposed tokens in a single forward pass using its full context, unlike ARM speculative decoding which requires sequential verification. We further propose an adaptive masking schedule that concentrates denoising steps on uncertain token positions identified by draft model confidence scores, reducing total steps while preserving quality. Experiments: We evaluate on LLaDA-8B against baselines including standard MDLM sampling, measuring throughput (tokens/second), latency, and quality (perplexity, downstream benchmarks including math and code) across varying draft model sizes (0.5B, 1B, 3B). We target 3-5x wall-clock speedup with less than 1% quality degradation.

title: Speculative Decoding for Masked Diffusion Language Models via Draft-then-Denoise
description: Problem: LLaDA and similar masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) suffer from slow inference because they require many sequential denoising steps (typically 64-256 forward passes) to generate high-quality text, making them impractical for latency-sensitive applications compared to single-pass ARM decoding. Unlike ARMs, MDLMs cannot directly benefit from standard speculative decoding since they lack a causal structure. Proposed Method: We introduce Draft-then-Denoise (DtD), a speculative acceleration framework tailored for MDLMs. A small, fast draft diffusion model (e.g., 1B parameters) performs coarse denoising in few steps, proposing a nearly-complete token sequence. A large verifier MDLM (e.g., 8B) then evaluates all proposed tokens in a single parallel forward pass, accepting high-confidence tokens and re-masking uncertain ones for targeted re-denoising. We derive acceptance criteria based on token-level marginal likelihood ratios from both models, ensuring the output distribution remains close to the large model's target distribution. A learned confidence threshold dynamically decides which tokens need re-denoising. Experiments: We evaluate on LLaDA-8B as the verifier with a distilled LLaDA-1B draft, measuring wall-clock speedup, perplexity, and task accuracy across summarization, math reasoning, and dialogue benchmarks, targeting 3-5x speedup with <1% quality degradation.

title: Speculative Diffusion Decoding: Accelerating Large Language Diffusion Models via Draft-and-Verify Sampling
description: Problem: Despite LLaDA's promising capabilities, masked diffusion language models suffer from slow inference because each denoising step requires a full forward pass through a large Transformer, and typically hundreds of steps are needed to generate high-quality sequences. This latency gap versus autoregressive models limits practical deployment. Proposed Method: We introduce Speculative Diffusion Decoding (SDD), adapting speculative decoding principles to the discrete diffusion setting. A small, fast draft diffusion model (e.g., LLaDA 1B) proposes tentative token unmaskings over multiple steps simultaneously, while the large verifier model (LLaDA 8B) evaluates the joint likelihood of the proposed tokens in a single forward pass and accepts or rejects them based on a corrected acceptance criterion derived from the diffusion likelihood lower bound. When proposals are rejected, the verifier corrects them in place without restarting the denoising trajectory. We additionally explore adaptive step-size scheduling guided by token confidence to further reduce verification calls. Experiments: We benchmark SDD on MT-Bench dialogue, GSM8K math, and HumanEval code generation, measuring wall-clock speedup, token acceptance rate, and quality degradation versus standard LLaDA sampling. We compare against naive step-reduction baselines and analyze the draft-verifier capacity ratio tradeoff, targeting 2–4× speedup with less than 1% quality loss.

title: SpecDiff: Accelerating Large Language Diffusion Models via Speculative Decoding with Autoregressive Draft Models
description: Problem: While LLaDA demonstrates that masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) are competitive with autoregressive models, their inference is slow because each denoising step requires a full forward pass through a large Transformer over all token positions simultaneously. Unlike ARMs, which benefit from KV-caching and speculative decoding, MDLMs lack dedicated acceleration strategies tailored to their iterative unmasking process. Proposed Method: We introduce SpecDiff, a speculative decoding framework for MDLMs. A small, fast autoregressive draft model proposes candidate token sequences, which are then verified in parallel by the larger MDLM (e.g., LLaDA 8B) in a single forward pass. Because MDLMs natively evaluate full-sequence likelihoods without causal masking, they can simultaneously verify multiple draft tokens across all positions, making them naturally suited as verifiers. We design an acceptance criterion based on the MDLM's masked token probabilities and a rejection-sampling correction to preserve the target distribution. We further explore using a small MDLM as both drafter and verifier in a cascaded setup. Experiments: We benchmark SpecDiff on LLaDA 8B across instruction-following (MT-Bench), math (GSM8K, MATH), and code (HumanEval) tasks, measuring tokens-per-second speedup, acceptance rates, and output quality degradation versus standard MDLM sampling, comparing against naive parallel decoding baselines.

title: DiffuRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Masked Diffusion Language Models
description:
Problem: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with autoregressive LLMs suffers from a fundamental tension: retrieved context must be processed left-to-right, preventing the model from dynamically reconciling conflicts between parametric knowledge and retrieved evidence during generation. Diffusion LMs like LLaDA, which denoise all output tokens jointly, offer a natural mechanism to iteratively refine answers in light of retrieved passages—but no work has explored RAG under the masked diffusion paradigm.

Proposed Method: We adapt LLaDA for RAG by (1) designing a retrieval-conditioned denoising objective where retrieved documents are prepended as unmasked context, and (2) introducing a confidence-guided remasking schedule that selectively re-masks low-confidence tokens whose predictions conflict with retrieved evidence across diffusion steps. We further propose iterative retrieval: after partial denoising, we re-query the retriever using the partially-denoised output as an updated query, enabling multi-hop reasoning through diffusion steps.

Experiments: We evaluate on Natural Questions, TriviaQA, HotpotQA (multi-hop), and PopQA (knowledge-intensive). Baselines include RAG with LLaMA3-8B, REPLUG, and Self-RAG. Ablations isolate the remasking strategy and iterative retrieval contributions. We also analyze faithfulness to retrieved context vs. parametric knowledge under conflicting evidence scenarios, hypothesizing diffusion's bidirectional denoising yields better conflict resolution than autoregressive decoding.

title: SpecDiff: Accelerating Large Language Diffusion Models via Speculative Decoding with Autoregressive Draft Models
description: Problem: While LLaDA demonstrates that masked diffusion language models are competitive with autoregressive LLMs, their inference remains slow because each denoising step requires a full forward pass through a large Transformer to unmask tokens, and many steps are needed for high-quality generation. Unlike autoregressive models, diffusion LLMs lack efficient speculative decoding frameworks tailored to their iterative unmasking process. Proposed Method: We introduce SpecDiff, a speculative acceleration framework for masked diffusion LLMs. A small, fast autoregressive draft model proposes candidate token sequences for a subset of masked positions at each diffusion timestep. The large diffusion model then verifies all proposed tokens in parallel during its standard denoising forward pass, accepting tokens that fall within a probabilistic acceptance criterion derived from the diffusion model's posterior. Rejected positions are resampled from the diffusion model's distribution, maintaining the exact generative distribution. We additionally propose a timestep-adaptive drafting schedule that increases draft aggressiveness at high-noise timesteps (where many tokens are masked) and reduces it at low-noise timesteps. Experiments: We evaluate on LLaDA 8B measuring wall-clock speedup (targeting 2-4x) versus standard diffusion sampling, text quality (perplexity, benchmark accuracy on MMLU/GSM8K), and acceptance rates across timesteps. Baselines include MDLM, PLAID, and standard diffusion sampling without speculation.

title: DiffEdit-Code: Leveraging Bidirectional Context in Large Language Diffusion Models for Repository-Level Code Editing
description:
Problem: Repository-level code editing requires understanding bidirectional dependencies—a function's callers, callees, type signatures, and surrounding context—which autoregressive models struggle with due to their left-to-right generation bias. Existing code LLMs treat edits as append-only completions, poorly suited for in-place modification tasks like refactoring, bug fixing, or API migration across files.

Proposed Method: We fine-tune LLaDA on a repository-level code editing task by framing edits as masked diffusion: given a code snippet with target lines masked (based on diff hunks), the model fills in the edit using full bidirectional context from surrounding code, docstrings, type annotations, and cross-file imports. We introduce a structured masking curriculum that progressively increases edit complexity (single-line → multi-hunk → cross-file). We augment training with synthetic edit pairs mined from GitHub commit histories, pairing pre- and post-commit code as (masked, target) pairs. A retrieval-augmented context window provides relevant file snippets at inference time.

Experiments: We evaluate on SWE-bench Verified, RepoBench-E (edit subset), and a new RealEdit-500 benchmark we construct from recent PyPI library migrations. Baselines include CodeLlama, Qwen2.5-Coder (ARM), and MDLM. Metrics: exact match, compilation success, test pass rate, and edit precision/recall. We ablate masking strategy, context window size, and diffusion steps.

title: DiffRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Masked Diffusion Language Models for Knowledge-Intensive Tasks
description: Problem: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with autoregressive LLMs suffers from a fundamental tension between retrieved context and generation: ARMs process retrieved documents sequentially and can be distracted by irrelevant passages placed early in context. Masked diffusion language models like LLaDA, which generate all output tokens simultaneously through iterative denoising, offer a structural advantage—they can attend to retrieved evidence bidirectionally and holistically during generation rather than left-to-right. This potential has not been explored. Proposed Method: We adapt LLaDA for RAG by designing a retrieval-conditioned denoising objective where the model learns to unmask answer tokens while jointly attending to multiple retrieved passages. We introduce a passage-relevance reweighting mechanism in the denoising process that dynamically suppresses noisy retrievals by modulating attention based on intermediate denoising confidence. We also propose a RAG-specific SFT protocol using (query, retrieved passages, answer) triples that teaches the model to reconcile conflicting evidence across passages. Experiments: We evaluate on standard knowledge-intensive benchmarks (Natural Questions, TriviaQA, PopQA, FEVER), multi-hop reasoning (HotpotQA, MuSiQue), and conflicting-evidence robustness tests. We compare against RAG-augmented LLaMA3 8B and GPT-4o under identical retrieval conditions, measuring accuracy, faithfulness, and robustness to irrelevant retrieved passages.

title: Speculative Decoding for Masked Diffusion Language Models via Confidence-Guided Token Scheduling
description: Problem: While LLaDA demonstrates that masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) can match autoregressive LLMs in quality, their inference remains slow due to requiring many sequential denoising steps, each invoking a full forward pass. Unlike ARMs where speculative decoding accelerates inference via draft-then-verify, no analogous acceleration framework exists for MDLMs. Proposed Method: We introduce DiffSpec, a confidence-guided speculative scheduling framework for MDLMs. At each denoising step, the model predicts token probabilities; DiffSpec identifies high-confidence tokens (those whose predicted distribution entropy falls below a learned threshold) and freezes them early, skipping their computation in subsequent steps via token-level early exit. Additionally, we train a lightweight 'draft diffusion' model that proposes multi-token unmasking candidates verified in parallel by the full MDLM, exploiting the non-sequential nature of diffusion generation. The threshold and draft model are jointly optimized to maximize throughput subject to a perplexity constraint. Experiments: (1) Measure wall-clock speedup vs. standard LLaDA inference on standard benchmarks (MT-Bench, GSM8K, HumanEval); (2) Compare quality degradation against ARM speculative decoding baselines; (3) Ablate freezing schedules and draft model sizes; (4) Evaluate scaling behavior from 1B to 8B parameters. We target 2-3x speedup with <1% quality degradation.

title: Speculative Decoding for Masked Diffusion Language Models via Confidence-Guided Token Scheduling
description: Problem: Large masked diffusion language models like LLaDA suffer from slow inference because they require many sequential denoising steps (e.g., 64-256 forward passes), each involving a full Transformer computation over the entire sequence. Unlike autoregressive models, there is no established acceleration framework tailored to masked diffusion LMs that exploits token-level confidence heterogeneity. Proposed Method: We introduce DiffSpec, a speculative execution framework for masked diffusion LMs. At each denoising step, a small draft network (e.g., a 1B parameter masked diffusion model) proposes token identities and confidence scores for all currently masked positions. A verification pass by the larger model (8B) then accepts high-confidence tokens immediately while re-masking low-confidence ones, effectively collapsing multiple denoising steps into one. We further introduce an adaptive step-skipping schedule that predicts, based on current mask density and entropy, whether intermediate steps can be safely skipped entirely. Planned Experiments: (1) Measure tokens-per-second speedup vs. standard LLaDA on diverse benchmarks (MT-Bench, GSM8K, HumanEval). (2) Evaluate quality degradation via perplexity and exact-match accuracy under varying acceptance thresholds. (3) Ablate draft model size (125M, 400M, 1B). (4) Compare against naive step-reduction baselines. Target: 3-5x wall-clock speedup with <1% quality loss.

title: Speculative Decoding for Masked Diffusion Language Models via Draft-and-Refine Token Proposal
description:
Problem: Large masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) like LLaDA generate text through iterative denoising over many steps, making inference significantly slower than autoregressive models. Unlike ARMs, MDLMs lack efficient speculative decoding frameworks because their parallel, non-sequential generation process is fundamentally different. This bottleneck limits practical deployment despite competitive quality.

Proposed Method: We introduce DiffSpec, a speculative decoding framework tailored for MDLMs. A small, fast draft MDLM proposes token assignments for heavily masked positions in few denoising steps. The larger target MDLM then verifies all proposed tokens simultaneously in a single forward pass—exploiting the natural parallelism of the masked prediction objective. We derive an acceptance criterion grounded in the MDLM likelihood lower bound to ensure the output distribution matches the target model exactly. Additionally, we propose an adaptive masking schedule that concentrates compute on high-uncertainty tokens identified by the draft model, further reducing target model calls.

Experiments: (1) Throughput benchmarks comparing DiffSpec against standard MDLM decoding and ARM speculative decoding on LLaDA-8B; (2) Quality evaluations on MT-Bench, HumanEval, and GSM8K confirming distribution preservation; (3) Ablations on draft model size, number of denoising steps, and masking schedules; (4) Analysis of acceptance rates across task types to characterize where draft-refine is most beneficial.

title: DiffEdit-Code: Masked Diffusion Language Models for Iterative Program Repair and Refinement
description: Problem: Autoregressive LLMs struggle with program repair tasks because fixing bugs often requires non-sequential, localized edits across a codebase—a fundamentally non-left-to-right operation. Iterative refinement via autoregressive models requires regenerating entire sequences, wasting computation on correct code regions. Proposed Method: We adapt LLaDA's masked diffusion framework specifically for program repair by introducing a bug-aware masking curriculum. Rather than uniformly masking tokens during pre-training, we design structured masking that preferentially masks syntactically meaningful code units (function bodies, variable names, conditionals) identified via AST analysis. During inference, we introduce a 'diagnostic-guided unmasking' procedure: static analysis tools (linters, type checkers, test failures) provide localized error signals that bias the reverse diffusion process to concentrate denoising iterations on buggy regions, leaving correct code untouched. This exploits diffusion's natural ability to perform partial sequence regeneration. Experiments: We evaluate on CodeNet, SWE-bench, and HumanEval-Fix benchmarks, comparing against CodeLlama, DeepSeek-Coder, and standard LLaDA. Ablations examine (1) structured vs. uniform masking curricula, (2) diagnostic-guided vs. uniform unmasking, and (3) multi-round repair iterations. We hypothesize that diffusion's bidirectional context and localized editing capabilities yield superior repair accuracy with fewer tokens regenerated per fix.

title: Speculative Diffusion Decoding: Accelerating Masked Diffusion Language Models with Lightweight Draft Models
description: Problem: Large masked diffusion language models like LLaDA require many sequential denoising steps (each requiring a full forward pass through a large Transformer) to generate text, making inference significantly slower than autoregressive models which benefit from KV-caching and speculative decoding techniques. This latency gap limits practical deployment of diffusion LLMs. Proposed Method: We introduce Speculative Diffusion Decoding (SDD), which pairs a large diffusion model (verifier) with a small, fast draft diffusion model trained to propose token unmaskings across multiple positions simultaneously. At each denoising step, the draft model proposes candidate unmaskings for a large subset of masked tokens; the large verifier model then evaluates all proposals in a single forward pass, accepting high-confidence unmaskings and re-masking rejected tokens. We develop a theoretically grounded acceptance criterion that preserves the target distribution of the original diffusion model. We further explore using a small ARM as the draft model, leveraging its speed advantage for initial token proposals. Experiments: We evaluate SDD on LLaDA-8B across standard benchmarks (text generation, math, instruction-following), measuring wall-clock speedup, acceptance rates, and quality degradation. We compare against baseline multi-step diffusion, MDLM, and ARM speculative decoding, targeting 2-4x inference speedup with minimal quality loss.

title: Speculative Diffusion Decoding: Accelerating Large Language Diffusion Models with Draft-then-Refine Masked Sampling
description: Problem: Despite LLaDA's competitive capabilities, masked diffusion language models suffer from slow inference because they require many sequential denoising steps (each involving a full forward pass through a large Transformer), making them impractical for latency-sensitive applications compared to cached autoregressive models. Proposed Method: We introduce Speculative Diffusion Decoding (SDD), which pairs a small draft diffusion model with the large target diffusion model. At each denoising timestep, the small model proposes a full token unmasking proposal across all positions simultaneously; the large model then evaluates acceptance probabilities in a single batched forward pass using a token-level rejection sampling scheme adapted for the masked diffusion framework. Accepted tokens are committed while rejected positions are re-masked and refined by the large model. We derive theoretical guarantees showing SDD preserves the exact marginal distribution of the target model. We further introduce an adaptive timestep scheduling strategy that concentrates large-model calls at high-uncertainty denoising steps. Experiments: We benchmark on standard generation tasks (MT-Bench, HumanEval, GSM8K) measuring wall-clock speedup and output quality parity against vanilla LLaDA-8B, compare against ARM speculative decoding baselines, and ablate draft model size, rejection threshold, and timestep allocation. We target 2-4x latency reduction with negligible quality degradation.

title: Speculative Diffusion Decoding: Accelerating Masked Diffusion Language Models with Lightweight Draft Models
description: Problem: Despite strong capabilities, large masked diffusion language models like LLaDA suffer from slow inference because they require many sequential denoising steps over the full sequence, making deployment impractical compared to autoregressive models that benefit from KV-caching and speculative decoding. Method: We propose Speculative Diffusion Decoding (SDD), a framework that accelerates masked diffusion LMs by pairing a large target diffusion model with a small draft diffusion model. The draft model rapidly proposes token unmaskings across multiple positions in fewer denoising steps, while the large model verifies and corrects proposals in parallel. We design a novel acceptance-rejection criterion adapted to the discrete masked diffusion framework, preserving the target model's marginal distribution. We also introduce an adaptive step scheduler that allocates more denoising steps to high-uncertainty token positions identified by the draft model. Experiments: We evaluate SDD on LLaDA 8B paired with a 1B draft model across standard benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K, HumanEval) and open-ended generation tasks, measuring wall-clock speedup, token throughput, and quality degradation. We compare against naive step-reduction baselines and analyze the acceptance rate as a function of draft-target capacity gap, targeting 2-4x practical speedup with less than 1% quality loss.

title: Speculative Diffusion Decoding: Accelerating Masked Diffusion Language Models via Draft-Then-Denoise
description:
Problem: Large masked diffusion language models like LLaDA achieve competitive quality but suffer from slow inference due to requiring many sequential denoising steps (typically 64-128 forward passes), making them impractical compared to autoregressive models with KV-cache acceleration. Unlike ARMs, existing speculative decoding methods don't transfer directly to diffusion models.

Proposed Method: We introduce Speculative Diffusion Decoding (SDD), a framework that uses a small, fast draft diffusion model to propose partially-denoised token sequences, which are then verified and corrected by the large target diffusion model in a single forward pass. We exploit the unique structure of masked diffusion: the draft model proposes confident token predictions at high-noise timesteps, while the target model selectively re-masks and corrects low-confidence positions. We additionally propose an adaptive timestep scheduling strategy where the acceptance rate of draft tokens guides dynamic allocation of denoising steps per token position.

Experiments: (1) Latency benchmarks on LLaDA-8B vs. LLaDA-1B draft pairs measuring tokens/second versus quality tradeoff; (2) Quality evaluation on standard benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K, HumanEval) comparing SDD against baseline full-step diffusion; (3) Ablations on draft model size, number of denoising steps, and acceptance threshold; (4) Comparison against ARM speculative decoding at matched quality levels.

title: SpecDiff: Accelerating Large Language Diffusion Models via Speculative Denoising with Autoregressive Draft Models
description: Problem: LLaDA and similar masked diffusion language models require many sequential denoising steps (e.g., 64-128 forward passes) during inference, making them significantly slower than autoregressive models despite comparable quality. This inference bottleneck limits practical deployment. Proposed Method: We introduce SpecDiff, a speculative decoding framework adapted for masked diffusion models. A small, fast autoregressive draft model (e.g., 1B parameter GPT-style) proposes a full token sequence in one pass. The large diffusion model (e.g., LLaDA 8B) then acts as a verifier: in a single denoising step, it computes token-level confidence scores over the draft and selectively rejects low-confidence tokens, re-masking and re-denoising only those positions. Accepted high-confidence tokens are kept, dramatically reducing the number of required diffusion steps. We develop a theoretical acceptance criterion grounded in the diffusion model's masking likelihood to ensure the output distribution remains unbiased. Experiments: We evaluate on standard benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K, HumanEval, MT-Bench), measuring tokens/second, quality degradation vs. standard diffusion decoding, and acceptance rates across rejection thresholds. We compare against naive step-reduction baselines and analyze how draft model size affects the speed-quality tradeoff, targeting 3-5x wall-clock speedup with <1% quality loss.

title: DiffRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Masked Diffusion Language Models for Knowledge-Intensive Tasks
description: Problem: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with autoregressive LLMs suffers from positional bias and sequential integration of retrieved context, often failing to coherently reconcile multiple retrieved documents with parametric knowledge. Masked diffusion language models like LLaDA offer a fundamentally different generation paradigm that can iteratively refine entire outputs holistically, potentially better integrating retrieved evidence across the full response simultaneously. Method: We adapt LLaDA for RAG by designing a retrieval-conditioned masked diffusion process where retrieved document chunks serve as unmasked conditioning anchors within the reverse diffusion trajectory. We introduce a retrieval-aware noise schedule that preserves tokens near retrieved evidence longer during diffusion, encouraging the model to build responses outward from factual anchors. We further propose a multi-step reranking mechanism that re-retrieves documents at intermediate denoising steps based on partially unmasked outputs, enabling dynamic retrieval refinement. Experiments: We evaluate on KILT benchmarks (TriviaQA, HotpotQA, FEVER, ELI5), multi-hop QA (MuSiQue, 2WikiMultiHopQA), and long-form generation (ASQA). We compare against ARM-based RAG baselines (LLaMA3, Mistral) with identical retrievers. Ablations examine the retrieval-anchor noise schedule and dynamic re-retrieval. We hypothesize LLaDA-RAG better handles contradictory retrieved documents due to its global denoising perspective.
